cleared.check: L-1031 probe set: 39 read-only probes (stack underflow, invalid jumps including into push data, out of gas, 0xfe, undefined 0x0c, TLOAD underflow, revert data, GAS after cold and warm SLOAD, a CALL to an empty account and a cold BALANCE, failed and absent precompiles 0x01, 0x05, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x100, read precompile 0x807, eth_estimateGas on a call that reverts at exactly one gas value and on a monotonic one, state against stateDiff overrides on the PoolManager, block context, and eth_call by block hash, old number, pending and a nonexistent hash), run on 2026-11-26 against rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm ('hyperliquid evm Mainnet', blocks 52,292,037 to 52,292,056), rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31), rpc.hyperlend.finance (reth/v0.1.0-b92ad36), and on Ethereum ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc), eth.blockrazor.xyz (Geth/v1.17.5-stable-3844b69e) and eth.rpc.blxrbdn.com (Geth/v1.16.7-stable-d62ed61f). Each run is bracketed with web3_clientVersion and eth_blockNumber.
cleared.result: The official endpoint answers like the revm and reth family on every probe where the families differ. On the eight error probes it returns the reth texts and code -32003 ('EVM error: StackUnderflow', 'EVM error: InvalidJump', 'out of gas: gas required exceeds: 100000', 'EVM error: InvalidFEOpcode', 'EVM error: OpcodeNotFound'), the same strings as f0cad31 and reth v2.11.0, where both geth builds say 'stack underflow (0 <=> 2)', 'invalid jump destination', 'out of gas' and 'invalid opcode: INVALID' with code -32000. It equals f0cad31 on all 30 probes that do not depend on the moment of the call, including eth_estimateGas results that no Ethereum client gives (0x536a, 0x535e and 0x1185a, where reth v2.11.0 says 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x11670 and geth 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x116f5), the same rejection text for an override with both state and stateDiff, and ECRECOVER priced at 15,000 gas (gas difference 0x3b19 against 0xc39 on Ethereum), which is nanoreth's HlSpecId::V2 multiplied precompile price. Opcode results, cold and warm access gas (0xef036, 0xee7fb, 0xee790, 0xedd50, 0xed321 everywhere), failed precompiles that consume all forwarded gas, and the absence of Prague and Osaka precompiles 0x0b and 0x100 also agree. The nine probes that differ all describe the call context: the official endpoint runs eth_call in a block numbered latest plus one with the parent's timestamp and hash chain (BLOCKHASH(NUMBER-1) equals the hash of the latest block on both endpoints), a gas limit of 30,000,000, ignores the block argument (an old number, a block hash, 'pending' and a nonexistent hash all give the latest-plus-one context), and returns a live HyperCore oracle value from 0x807 (0x93fda) where f0cad31 forwards an unrecorded call and returns 0x93fe4 and b92ad36 halts out of gas. So official eth_call runs revm, behind reth's RPC types, inside a process that holds live HyperCore state. The node README states that the same hl-node binary runs run-validator and run-non-validator and that --serve-eth-rpc serves this RPC; whether the RPC path calls the same execution code that builds blocks cannot be seen from outside, and the hl-node binary itself was not obtainable (binaries.hyperliquid.xyz/Mainnet/hl-node answered HTTP 403). None of the context differences reaches src/: the PoolManager reads no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH, BASEFEE, PREVRANDAO or GASPRICE and calls no precompile; its only gas reads are the forwarded gas of three calls.

cleared.check: Whether the HyperEVM V2 precompile repricing that the probe set shows (ECRECOVER at 15,000 gas on the official endpoint and on both replicas) or the 30,000,000 gas limit of the official eth_call context changes any result of src/.
cleared.result: src/ calls no precompile. The only gas reads are call(gas(), ...) in src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, which forward all remaining gas, so a price change can make a transaction run out of gas but cannot change a value it computes. Quotes simulated on the official endpoint run in a 30,000,000 gas context while small blocks hold 3,000,000, so a swap that simulates can fail when mined; that is gas only and the failing transaction reverts as a whole.

leads.question: Rerun follow mode (scripts/follow.py) during a window with PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity activity, so that at least one write to slot0, liquidity, a tick or a position is read on the official endpoint while it is still the latest value.
leads.why: The 20 minute window of this cycle held no PoolManager write, and the newest one is 26,000 blocks old, so no intermediate word was compared.

leads.question: Does the Hyperliquid team state whether rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm is served by hl-node --serve-eth-rpc, and whether that RPC executes through the same EVM function the validator uses to build blocks?
leads.why: The probe set shows revm inside a node with live HyperCore state but cannot show that the code path is the producer's. That one statement decides how much the 185,529 vectors say about the closed validator.

leadResults.answer: The official endpoint's eth_call is revm behind reth's RPC types: it matches nanoreth f0cad31 on all 30 probes not tied to the time of the call, and matches reth rather than geth on all 8 probes where the families differ. It is not a nanoreth replica: it executes in a latest-plus-one context, ignores the block argument, and serves live HyperCore read precompile values that only a node with HyperCore state has. That fits hl-node run with --serve-eth-rpc, which the node README documents and which is the same binary validators run. It does not prove that eth_call calls the block-building code path of the validator, so the 185,529 vectors speak for revm inside hl-node with that caveat. The branch and edge coverage part of this lead belongs to theme-producer-branch-coverage and was not repeated here.

Follow mode ran from 11:35 to 11:55 UTC on 2026-11-26 over 619 blocks (52,293,163 to 52,294,373): 62 loops over the 205 words of the 12 pools with the latest Swap or ModifyLiquidity logs, 12,703 pinned reads, all equal to f0cad31 at the bracket block, no unpinned batch. No PoolManager log appeared in the window, and the newest PoolManager log on chain is at block 52,266,493, so no write was caught. Per-block validator output that is public is the receipt: nanoreth re-executes every block and checks gas used, the receipts root and the logs bloom against the validator's header (F-120 sources). Each Swap log carries the sqrtPriceX96, liquidity and tick that the swap wrote to slot0 and liquidity (src/PoolManager.sol:241, src/libraries/Pool.sol:439-442), and the PoolManager's other words are read-modify-write (src/libraries/Pool.sol:226, :474-477, src/libraries/Position.sol:88, :100, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47), so a wrong intermediate word would change the latest word or a later receipt unless a later full overwrite such as clearTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:592-593) erased it without any read in between. That residue is unmeasured.

8,867 items (8,464 slots, 86 bitmap words between the start and end tick of every mined swap, native balance, 316 balanceOf) agree between the official endpoint and f0cad31 at blocks 52,292,458 to 52,292,893. The gas price 0 census over 12,000 further contiguous blocks found 4,620 system transactions, none touching the PoolManager. No new PoolManager log was emitted since cycle 23, so no fresh swap was available to exercise.

The aligned quote assets page and the exchange endpoint page fetched on 2026-11-26 are byte identical to the cycle 23 copies (sha256 9fd997fe... and 812ecf7e...). The page says the treasury deployer, who stakes 500,000 HYPE, designates the treasury address; authorizeAqav2Role takes only token and role; no page states a rule against an address with code or names another path that sets the treasury address. Secondary news reports name 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00 as the USDC treasury, which has no code on the official endpoint (nonce 1,071,295 at block 52,292,536); 0x4e5319deb1072b01439ee674db5c321d11fd96f8, named in one report, has no code and nonce 4. The PoolManager nonce is still 1. No documented path lets an ordinary account set the treasury address, so F-020 stays plausible, high, operator.
